easy.explanation: The verse begins, “The words of Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah.”
easy.q: Who introduces the words at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “in the month Chisleu.”
easy.q: In which month did these events take place?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah says, “as I was in Shushan the palace.”

answers: The year after the wall was built
medium.explanation: The verse identifies the time as “the twentieth year.”
medium.q: What detail gives the year of the event?

medium.explanation: In this setting, “the palace” refers to the royal citadel.
medium.q: What does “the palace” mean in “Shushan the palace”?

answers: To introduce Nehemiah and establish the time and place
medium.explanation: The verse introduces Nehemiah and gives the month, year, and location.
medium.q: What is the main purpose of verse 1?

answers: A name, a time, and a place
A prayer, a fast, and a city
A king, a battle, and a gate
challenge.explanation: The verse gives Nehemiah’s name, the month and year, and Shushan the palace.
challenge.q: Which combination of details appears in verse 1?

answers: That the events begin in Jerusalem
That Nehemiah was in a specific royal setting
That Nehemiah had already arrived in Judah
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah states that he was in Shushan the palace.
challenge.q: What does the opening location show?

challenge.explanation: The condition of the walls is reported in verses 2–3.
challenge.q: Which detail is not mentioned in verse 1?

short_answers.question: Where was Nehemiah when these events took place?
short_answers.answer: He was in Shushan the palace.
short_answers.explanation: Nehemiah identifies Shushan the palace as his location.

paragraphs.title: The Report about Judah and Jerusalem

answers: Hanani and certain men of Judah
Moses and the children of Israel
The king of Jerusalem and his servants
easy.explanation: Hanani came with certain men of Judah.
Nehemiah asked about the Jews and concerning Jerusalem.
The report says, “the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down.”
easy.q: What was the condition of Jerusalem’s wall?

medium.explanation: The remnant was in “great affliction and reproach.”
medium.q: What condition of the Jews was reported?

answers: Both were in a troubled condition
Only the Jews were in trouble
medium.explanation: The Jews suffered affliction, while the wall and gates of Jerusalem were ruined.
medium.q: What relationship does the report show between the Jews and Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes a wall that had been broken and left with breaches.
medium.q: What does “broken down” mean in the report about the wall?

answers: Its gates were burned with fire
challenge.explanation: The report says, “the gates thereof are burned with fire.”
challenge.q: What additional detail is given about Jerusalem’s destruction?

challenge.explanation: He asked in order to know how the people and city were doing.
challenge.q: Why did Nehemiah ask about the Jews and Jerusalem?

answers: The gates were rebuilt, and then the people suffered
The Jews were in distress, and the wall and gates were ruined
Nehemiah prayed, and then Hanani arrived
challenge.explanation: The men reported distress among the Jews and destruction in Jerusalem.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes the report?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days.”
easy.q: How did Nehemiah respond when he heard the report?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah says that he “fasted, and prayed.”
easy.q: What else did Nehemiah do besides mourn?

easy.explanation: He prayed “before the God of heaven.”

answers: The report about the Jews and Jerusalem
medium.explanation: His response followed the troubling words he had heard.
medium.q: What caused Nehemiah to weep and mourn?

medium.explanation: Nehemiah confessed or acknowledged the sins of Israel.
medium.q: What does “confess” mean in this passage?

answers: Only the sins of the people in Judah
The sins of Israel, including himself and his father’s house
medium.explanation: He says, “both I and my father’s house have sinned.”

answers: He heard, wept and mourned, fasted, and prayed
He prayed, heard, and then wept
He fasted, departed, and then heard
challenge.explanation: This is the order given in verse 4.

answers: He joined in the confession of the nation’s sins
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah included himself and his household in the confession.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah’s inclusion of himself and his father’s house show?

answers: The great and terrible God who keeps covenant and mercy
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah calls God great and terrible and says that He keeps covenant and mercy.
challenge.q: How is God described at the beginning of Nehemiah’s prayer?

paragraphs.title: Recalling the Warning and the Promise

easy.explanation: Nehemiah recalls the word commanded to Moses.
easy.q: To whom did God give the commandment that Nehemiah recalls?

answers: They would be scattered among the nations
easy.explanation: God said, “I will scatter you abroad among the nations.”
easy.q: What would happen if the people transgressed?

answers: Gather them and bring them to the chosen place
Drive them farther from the land
easy.explanation: God promised to gather them and bring them to the place He had chosen.
easy.q: What did God promise to do for those who returned to Him and kept His commandments?

answers: Turning to God and keeping His commandments
medium.explanation: The promise begins, “if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments.”
medium.q: What condition was connected with the promise of gathering?

answers: Being scattered to very distant places
medium.explanation: The phrase describes extreme distance and dispersion.
medium.q: What does “the uttermost part of the heaven” describe?

medium.explanation: Nehemiah says, “these are thy servants and thy people.”
medium.q: How did Nehemiah describe the people before God?

answers: Transgression leads to scattering among the nations
Transgression immediately leads to rebuilding Jerusalem
There is no relationship between them
challenge.explanation: God warned that transgression would result in scattering.
challenge.q: What relationship between sin and scattering is presented?

answers: Turning to God and keeping His commandments lead to the promised gathering
Turning to God causes further scattering
The prayer contains no promise of gathering
challenge.explanation: The promise of gathering follows the condition of turning to God and obeying Him.
challenge.q: What relationship between turning to God and gathering is presented?

answers: They were redeemed by God’s great power and strong hand
challenge.explanation: Nehemiah calls them the people whom God redeemed by His great power and strong hand.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah emphasize about the people’s past?

paragraphs.title: A Plea for Favor before the King

easy.explanation: He asks God to prosper him and grant him mercy.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah ask God to grant him?

easy.explanation: He asks for mercy “in the sight of this man.”
easy.q: Before whom did Nehemiah ask to find mercy?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah says, “I was the king’s cupbearer.”

answers: So he could act for the repair of Jerusalem
So he could leave his position
So he could punish the men of Judah
medium.explanation: His request prepared the way for action on behalf of Jerusalem.
medium.q: Why did Nehemiah ask for success before the king?

answers: A servant who attended the king and served his drink
A person who watered the city walls
A leader over the people of Judah
medium.explanation: A cupbearer served the king and held a trusted position near him.

answers: Those who desire to fear God’s name
medium.explanation: Nehemiah refers to servants who desire to fear God’s name.
medium.q: Who are “thy servants” in Nehemiah’s prayer?

answers: Nehemiah asks God to hear both his prayer and the prayer of His servants
Nehemiah does not mention other worshipers
challenge.explanation: He asks God to hear “the prayer of thy servant, and the prayer of thy servants.”
challenge.q: What connection is made between the people’s prayer and Nehemiah’s prayer?

answers: He was close to the king
challenge.explanation: The position of cupbearer placed him near the king.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Nehemiah’s occupation?

answers: Prayer, a request for success and mercy, and the identification of Nehemiah’s office
Building a wall, fighting a battle, and fasting
Arriving in Jerusalem, praying, and receiving the report
challenge.explanation: The verse contains a prayer, a request before the king, and Nehemiah’s statement that he was the king’s cupbearer.

short_answers.question: What office did Nehemiah hold?
short_answers.explanation: Nehemiah identifies his position at the end of the verse.

easy.explanation: He sat down, wept, mourned, fasted, and prayed.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah do after hearing the report?

easy.explanation: The text says that he fasted and prayed before God.
easy.q: What did Nehemiah do during his mourning?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah prayed before the God of heaven.
easy.q: To whom did Nehemiah direct his prayer?

medium.explanation: Reproach means shame, disgrace, or dishonor.
medium.q: What does the word “reproach” mean in the report?

answers: That the people had sinned against God
That the people had conquered Persia
That the people had never received commandments
medium.explanation: He confessed the sins of the children of Israel.
medium.q: What did Nehemiah acknowledge about Israel?

medium.explanation: He said, “both I and my father’s house have sinned.”
medium.q: What did Nehemiah say about his father’s house?

answers: He responds to national suffering with mourning, fasting, and prayer
He blames only the people of Judah
challenge.explanation: His response combines grief, spiritual discipline, and confession.

answers: The time needed to build the wall
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that he prayed continually.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “day and night” emphasize?

answers: He identifies himself with the people’s guilt
challenge.explanation: He includes himself and his father’s house in the confession.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah’s confession reveal about his attitude?

short_answers.question: Name two actions Nehemiah took after hearing the report.
short_answers.answer: He wept, mourned, fasted, and prayed; any two of these are correct.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 lists these responses to the report.
